newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy centre-right sees progress in budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy centre-right sees progress in budget talks.

text.p: Party leaders from Italy's centre-left government and centre-right opposition met for half an hour of talks on Monday over Prime Minister Romano Prodi's tough 1997 budget and the opposition said progress was possible.
Enrico La Loggia, leader of the centre-right Forza Italia party in the Senate (upper house), told reporters he saw "possible steps forward" on the controversial budgetary measures.

La Loggia said the party leaders would meet again at 1830 GMT. The centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc would in the meantime decide whether "these steps are such as to enable a change in our attitude". He declined to go into details.
He said the talks had only been about the budget and had focused on fiscal measures in particular.
Deputies of the Freedom Alliance, led by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, boycotted the budget debate in the lower Chamber of Deputies, where the budget passed without them.
The package is now before the Senate budget committee for discussion on proposed amendments.

Prodi's 1997 budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41.2 billion) off next year's deficit. A key element of the package is an unpopular "Euro-tax" to raise some 12.5 trillion lire to help Italy be a founder member of a European single currency. The tax was not part of the budget discussions in the Chamber. ($1=1,514 lire)
